ap_physics_1-m01.set_intro: The graph shows the position of a cart on a straight track as a function of time. Positive positions are to the right of the origin.

stimulus.description: Position of a cart versus time

items.stem: What is the velocity of the cart between $t=5\text{ s}$ and $t=8\text{ s}$? Positive is to the right.

options.why: Reports the speed of the longest segment of the trip instead of the segment asked about.
Reports the position at the end of the interval instead of the slope.
Reports the position change without dividing by the elapsed time.
The velocity is the slope of the graph: $(10-(6))/(8-5)=1.33\text{ m/s}$.

blueprint.subject: ap_physics_1
blueprint.concept: Two questions about a single position-time graph
student_thinking: Read the slope of the graph segment for the velocity
Add the magnitudes of the position changes between the plotted points for the distance and divide by the elapsed time for the average speed

key_conditions.condition: the position changes linearly between the plotted points
key_conditions.evidence: the graph is built from integer vertices joined by straight segments

misconceptions.description: Reports the speed of the longest segment of the trip instead of the segment asked about.
Reports the position at the end of the interval instead of the slope.
Reports the position change without dividing by the elapsed time.

verification.independent_path: exact fractions for the slope and the distance versus numpy on a dense resampling of the same graph

items.stem: What is the average speed of the cart for the whole trip from $t=0$ to $t=8\text{ s}$?

options.why: Divides the total distance by the duration of the longest segment.
Reports the average velocity (net displacement divided by time), which cancels the motion in opposite directions.
The total distance adds the magnitude of each position change, $18.0\text{ m}$, and dividing by $8\text{ s}$ gives $2.25\text{ m/s}$.
Adds the speeds of all the segments.

ap_physics_1-m02.set_intro: A $1.5\text{ kg}$ block slides across a rough horizontal floor and comes to rest. No other horizontal force acts on the block. The graph shows the velocity of the block as a function of time.

stimulus.description: Velocity of the block versus time

items.stem: What is the magnitude of the net force on the block while it slides?

options.why: The acceleration is the slope of the graph, $6/4=1.50\text{ m/s}^2$ in magnitude, so $F_{net}=ma=(1.5)(1.50)=2.25\text{ N}$.
Uses half of the slope as if it were an average acceleration.
Multiplies the mass by the stopping time.
Multiplies the mass by the initial speed, which is a momentum, not a force.

blueprint.subject: ap_physics_1
blueprint.concept: Two questions about a block that slides to a stop on a rough floor
student_thinking: Read the acceleration from the slope of the velocity-time graph
Apply Newton's second law with the kinetic friction force as the net force

key_conditions.condition: kinetic friction is the only horizontal force on the block
key_conditions.evidence: the shared stimulus states the block slides on a rough horizontal floor with no other horizontal force

misconceptions.description: Uses half of the slope as if it were an average acceleration.
Multiplies the mass by the stopping time.
Multiplies the mass by the initial speed, which is a momentum, not a force.

verification.independent_path: the slope from the graph endpoints; the net force from Newton's second law and the coefficient cross-checked with the stopping distance v0 squared over 2 mu g equal to the area under the graph

items.stem: What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the floor?

options.why: Friction is the only horizontal force, so $\mu mg=ma$ and $\mu=a/g=1.50/9.8=0.15$.
Divides $g$ by the acceleration, inverting the ratio.
Reports the magnitude of the acceleration, forgetting to divide by $g$.
Divides the acceleration by $2g$.
